title: Documentation support (MEAT) for chronic conditions
question: Which chronic condition, if any, is supported for risk adjustment by this note? Ignore the reason for the visit. Choose 'no code' if none is supported.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for persistent low back pain.

HPI
The patient is a 54-year-old male presenting for evaluation of chronic low back pain that has persisted for approximately three months. He reports a dull ache localized to the lumbar region, which occasionally radiates into the right buttock. He notes that the pain is exacerbated by prolonged sitting and heavy lifting. He denies any recent trauma, fever, or neurological deficits such as numbness or tingling in the lower extremities. He has attempted over-the-counter analgesics with only partial relief.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily
Tiotropium 18mcg daily
Naproxen 500mg as needed

Exam
The patient is alert and in no acute distress. Physical exam reveals tenderness to palpation over the lumbar spine. Range of motion is limited by discomfort. Straight leg raise test is negative bilaterally. Strength and sensation are intact in both lower extremities.

Assessment
1. Chronic low back pain.

Plan
The patient will begin a course of physical therapy twice weekly focusing on core strengthening and stretching. We discussed proper lifting techniques and ergonomic adjustments at his workplace. Follow-up in four weeks to assess progress.
explanations: An inhaler on the medication list does not establish COPD; coders do not infer diagnoses from medications.

distractors.why: Only the provider can document a diagnosis.
